newsitem.title: LATVIA: BUSINESS NEWSPAPER SEES LAT REVALUATION.
newsitem.headline: BUSINESS NEWSPAPER SEES LAT REVALUATION.

text.p: Latvian business newspaper Dienas Bizness said in its editorial on Wednesday that the lat may be revalued upwards.
The newspaper said that the most important argument backing such a forecast was the low rate on government Treasury bills.
It said that foreign investors were buying Latvian T-bills with an annual yield of four to five percent when it was more profitable to invest in U.S. paper at five to six percent.
It also said that a revaluation upwards would be favoured by some major Latvian food companies which have soon to begin to repay G24 credits in dollars but whose main income is in lats.

"Financial experts are unanimous in saying that the Bank of Latvia does not have to revalue the currenct itself but it would be enough to determine a freely-floating exchange rate," the newspaper said in its editorial.
The Latvian central bank yesterday said that the lat was undervalued in terms of purchasing power parity.
Central bank governor Einar Repshe also told Reuters in an interview last week that he believed the lat was slightly undervalued.
However, he said there would be no change in the central bank's policy of keeping the lat pegged to the SDR.
Dienas Bizness also quoted Latvia International Monetary Fund (IMF) representative Dimitri Demekas as saying there were no plans to revalue the lat.
"We do not see any signs in the basic economic indicators of Latvia which would force such a step," he told the newspaper, adding that he was surprised such talk had begun at all.
